content.text:
Japan and Korea customers should now be charged the invoice total, and `npm test` passes (7 of 7). I didn't commit anything.

**Root cause:** `buildChargePayload` in `src/payments/gateway/payload.js` lowercases the currency (`JPY` → `jpy`) because the gateway wants lower-case codes. It then passes that code to `toMinor`. The currency registry in `src/lib/currency/registry.js` only had upper-case keys, so `exponent('jpy')` found nothing and fell back to 2 decimals. ¥1,500 became 150,000. Zero-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW, VND, CLP) were affected. Three-decimal currencies (BHD, KWD) were also getting the wrong exponent. USD and EUR use 2 decimals, which matched the fallback, so they looked fine.

**Fix:** the registry lookups (`exponent`, `isSupported`, `symbol`) now trim and upper-case the code first. I fixed it there, not in `payload.js`, because other modules that call `toGatewayCurrency` or `toMinor` could hit the same problem.

**Regression test:** I added one to `test/charge.test.js`. It checks that a ¥1,500 JPY invoice produces `amount: 1500` and `currency: 'jpy'`, and that a ₩20,000 KRW invoice produces `20000`.

I didn't check whether any past JPY or KRW charges need refunding. Look at charges made while this was live.
